question.worked_solution:
First, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-2 \\ \lambda  & =\pm \sqrt{2}\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =P\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}x)+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}x)\end{aligned}
$$

We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(0)=-4$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}P=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=4\sqrt{2},$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-\sqrt{2}P\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}x)+\sqrt{2}Q\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}x).
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=4\sqrt{2}$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}Q=4\sqrt{2}\,⟹\,Q=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}x)+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}x).
$$
